rationale: Both of my round-1 asks are ADDRESSED as specified — re-derived against the tree at 99d75484, not the fix report. But the execution of ask 1 swapped repair's derivation from the status-aware DerivePhaseDetail to bare DerivePhaseFromChildren, and the spec itself (spec.md:99, round-4 G1.2) records that the bare form cannot express terminal rows: an all-closed lifecycle child set derives `review`, never `done` (re-confirmed at derive.go:344-378). Consequence, traced end-to-end: on any COMPLETED spec (stored `done`, epic closed with its done marker, all children closed) `mindspec repair phase` previously took the status-aware path (deriveFromChildrenOrStatusWithCache with fetched epic status -> hasDoneMarker -> `done`, derive.go:282-291) and printed 'already consistent: done', exit 0; at 99d75484 it derives `review` in-lock, IsBackwardMove(done, review)=true, and REFUSES with 'the epic genuinely regressed' plus a --force-backward suggestion — and an operator or agent who obeys that suggested lever would actively corrupt a healthy done epic back to `review`. repair is the ONE phase-fix lever every emitted recovery line names (repair.go's own Spec-092 header), bead 2 adds more emitted hints pointing at it, and ADR-0035's whole premise is that executing a recovery line improves state — so a spurious hard refusal with a corrupting force-suggestion on every shipped spec is a real regression, introduced by the round-1 fix and pinned by no test (repair_test.go has no done-epic fixture). This is a NEW_ISSUE under my own ask, not a MISSED — the freshness mechanics I asked for are exactly right; the derivation FUNCTION chosen inside the critical section is wrong for terminal states. The fix is one line plus one test: use the status-aware derivation with the fresh in-fn cache (phase.DerivePhaseDetailWithCache(c, epicID) is exported and cache-parameterized — take .Derived and ignore its Stored) and add the done-epic fixture asserting the already-consistent success path. Everything else under my lens is now right: the caller-obligation doc (phaselock.go:186-207) states both obligations I asked for almost verbatim; the (stored, present) signature is the right long-term shape for all four bead-2 consumers; present-but-invalid semantics are correct for the v2 marker work. go build + internal/phase -race + repair tests green; worktree left byte-identical, no phase.lock residue.
concrete_changes_required: cmd/mindspec/repair.go (repairPhaseRunE's fn): restore terminal-row correctness while keeping the in-critical-section freshness — derive via the status-aware surface using the fresh per-call cache already constructed inside fn (e.g. detail, derr := phase.DerivePhaseDetailWithCache(c, epicID); use detail.Derived, ignore detail.Stored in favor of the lock's fresh read), instead of bare phase.DerivePhaseFromChildren(children). Bare children derivation returns `review` for an all-closed set (derive.go:375), so at 99d75484 `mindspec repair phase` on a completed spec (stored `done`, closed epic, done marker) refuses as a backward move and suggests --force-backward — which, if obeyed, regresses a healthy done epic to `review`. Pre-fix behavior (both 5101a07a and main) correctly derived `done` and printed 'already consistent'. Add the pinning fixture: closed epic + mindspec_done marker + all-closed children -> repair exits 0 on the already-consistent path, no refusal, stored stays `done`.

findings.title: Round-1 ask 1 (derive inside the critical section): ADDRESSED — mechanics exactly as requested
findings.detail: repairPhaseRunE now derives inside WithPhaseWriteLock's fn with a fresh per-call phase.NewCache() (repair.go:245-252), the guard compares fresh-stored (the lock's presence-aware read) against fresh-derived, derivation failures propagate via errors.Is-matched sentinels (errRepairDerivationFailed/errRepairNoDerivedPhase) with the pre-existing recovery-line messaging preserved (bd show on derivation failure, re-run on write failure), and the doc comment now cites spec.md:113's pinned read-stored -> derive -> guard-compare -> MergeMetadata mechanism. The backward-concurrent-writer arm I traced in round 1 (release's sanctioned backward sync racing a forward-stale repair derivation) is structurally closed: repair's target can no longer predate the lock. AC-5(v)'s stale-target leg is preserved by driving staleness through the SetListJSONForTest children fixture, as I suggested. SanctionedDerivedSync additionally now propagates a failed children read instead of deriving from a nil slice (sanctioned_sync.go:55-58) — closing R6's hard-block hole that would have made a failed discovery a sanctioned backward write once bead 2 wires release.

findings.title: The in-lock derivation chose the terminal-row-blind surface: repair now spuriously refuses on every completed spec and suggests a corrupting --force-backward
findings.detail: The move inside the lock swapped DerivePhaseDetail (status-aware: closed epic + done marker -> `done`, derive.go:286-289) for bare DerivePhaseFromChildren (all-closed -> `review`, derive.go:375 — the exact terminal-row limitation spec.md:99/round-4 G1.2 documents). Trace on a shipped spec: stored `done`, fn derives `review`, IsBackwardMove(done, review)=true (phaseRank done=4 > review=3), no force flag -> guard.NewFailure 'stored phase "done" is ahead of the re-derived phase "review"... the epic genuinely regressed' with the --force-backward recovery suggestion; forcing would write `review` over a correct `done`. Before this fix commit the same invocation printed 'Phase for X already consistent: done' and exited 0. No test pins the done-epic row (grep of repair_test.go: none), so the regression is silent. Impact is contract-level for my lens: repair is the single emitted phase-fix lever (HC-5/Spec 092 Req 19) and bead 2's legacy notice adds another emitted path into it — an ADR-0035 recovery line whose execution can corrupt state inverts R3.2. One-line fix + one fixture, listed in concrete_changes_required.

findings.title: Round-1 ask 2 (caller-obligation doc): ADDRESSED — both obligations stated, with the house pattern named
findings.detail: phaselock.go:186-207 now carries exactly the two obligations I asked for: (1) freshness covers only the stored value + presence bit — every other decision input must be read inside fn with its own Cache, explicitly calling a pre-lock target closed over by fn 'a STALE read with respect to this lock, exactly the race this lock exists to close', and naming SanctionedDerivedSync and repair's guard as the house pattern; (2) non-reentrancy — nested acquisition (direct or transitive via SanctionedDerivedSync inside another fn) self-blocks to ErrPhaseLockTimeout. This is the paragraph that keeps bead 2's EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 author out of exactly the trap the round-2 regression in R3-r2-new1 shows is easy to fall into.

findings.title: The re-changed fn signature (stored string, present bool) IS the stable shape for bead 2's four consumers
findings.detail: Judged against each consumer: (1) next's new first-claim writer — needs 'no-op when already implement, forward write otherwise'; fn(stored, _) expresses it directly, and present-but-invalid (stored "", present true) safely takes the forward-write branch, overwriting garbage with a valid forward value. (2) plan-approve's value change — ignores both params, one-literal edit in the existing closure. (3) release wiring — SanctionedDerivedSync's exported signature is unchanged; the new releaseSyncPhase named function plus the exactly-one fence tightening (still a one-assertion change; sanctioned_sync_test.go untouched by the fix) slot in without rework. (4) EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 — the presence bit is exactly what its marker-absent/legacy-signature discrimination needs, and migrate.go:68-77 already models the pattern (backfill only on present==false). The comma-ok (value, bool) pair is the Go idiom; the churn risk of a second signature change is nil because nothing outside this bead has consumed it yet. readPhaseForLock deliberately NOT reusing readStoredPhaseWithCache is the right call — the wide read-only contract stays untouched while the lock gets the stricter error/presence-aware one.

findings.title: Present-but-invalid semantics: the right contract for the v2 marker work, with one doc nit
findings.detail: The three-way split (error propagates pre-fn; absent = present false; present-but-invalid = present true, stored "") is correct for bead 2: EnsureMigrated backfills ONLY genuine absence (migrate.go:76-78 — a garbage value is never silently laundered into a derived one), and EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2's legacy signature (stored == "implement" + child pattern) cannot false-fire on a corrupted value since stored reads "". Nit, informational: migrate.go's new comment calls repair phase 'the correct lever for a corrupted value', but on present-but-invalid repair's guard sees stored "" and IsBackwardMove("", derived) = true (order.go's conservative-unknown rule), so that lever REQUIRES --force-backward plus a reason. That force-gated audit trail for overwriting garbage is defensible — arguably desirable — but the comment reads as if plain repair suffices; a half-line ('via --force-backward, which is the point: overwriting a corrupted value deserves a recorded reason') would make it honest. Not verdict-driving.

findings.title: Collateral fix-commit surface under my lens: sound
findings.detail: DescribeLockFailure gives best-effort sync callers (releaseSyncPhase/completeSyncPhase) a surfaced, never-deleting ADR-0035 timeout treatment instead of round 1's discarded errors — the right contract for bead 2's release rewiring since SanctionedDerivedSync's error now MUST be surfaced somewhere. SetLockWaitForTest as package-level vars + restore func is the established house seam shape. The G2 repairFindRootFn seam fixes a real hermeticity hole (ambient findRoot walking up to the shared main checkout from a linked worktree — the round-1 hard-block's second driver) without changing the production path. Verified empirically at 99d75484: go build clean, internal/phase -race green, TestRepair* green, worktree byte-identical afterward with no phase.lock residue.
